title: Single-sequence tau calibration, reproduced and checked
body:
For a sequence query, `Profile::from_blosum_62_and_seq` in `libnail/src/structs/profile.rs` sets the forward tau from the sequence length L with a closed form, in place of the simulation hmmbuild runs to calibrate a model. This milestone reproduces the experiment that fit that closed form, checks each step, and sets the formula in nail from the result. The experiment is described here fully enough to run again from this text alone.

## The original experiment

A colleague of Jack's ran it, with files dated 2026-09-13. Jack keeps the archive at `~/Downloads/tau-calibration.zip` on the 16-core box.

- Sequences: `PTHR_190k.fasta`, 189,921 sequences from a random sample of 1,500 of the 15,683 family fastas in PANTHER 19.0, for training. `PTHR_190k_v2.fasta`, 193,872 sequences from a disjoint sample of 1,500 families, held out. The lists of sampled files are not in the archive.
- For each sequence: `hmmbuild --singlemx --seed N <out.hmm> <one-seq.fa>`, one sequence per file. tau is recorded as minus mu from the `STATS LOCAL FORWARD` line, so it is positive. lambda is from the same line.
- Runs: training at seeds 42 and 21, held-out at seed 42.
- Fit: least squares of tau = a*ln(L) + b on training at seed 42. A grid search around that fit then picked the two-decimal (a, b) with the least mean absolute error.
- Result: tau = 1.34*ln(L) - 2.33. Mean absolute error 0.185 on training, 0.186 held out. Seed 42 against seed 21 on the same sequences gives a mean absolute difference of 0.210.

nail's code does not use that result. Jack typed the formula in by hand in `a9900ba`. In the same sign convention it works out to tau = 1.317*ln(L) - 2.537, which sits 0.33 to 0.35 below hmmbuild on all three of the original data sets (nail-7c334f).

## Units

hmmbuild reports mu and lambda for bit scores. nail's `p_value(score, lambda, tau)` in `libnail/src/align/scoring.rs` returns exp(-lambda * (S - tau)) with S in bits. So a tau from hmmbuild goes into nail's `fwd_tau` as mu, which is minus the experiment's tau. For a score below tau that formula exceeds 1, where HMMER's exponential tail returns 1.

## The rerun

Done in `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-tau-calibration` on the 16-core box, with HMMER 3.4 (Aug 2023), 8 hmmbuild jobs at a time, `--cpu 1` each. The rerun reuses the original sequence files, which have these sha256 sums:

| file | sha256 |
|---|---|
| `PTHR_190k.fasta` | `717674d687c53526485893577012026ce7236ca0c7c9ce2f23e41a5b17ece289` |
| `PTHR_190k_v2.fasta` | `2b768e043a2d2e83254a1fe1e064cb7f8449467fea5aec2c14cd3099cc598b1e` |

The scripts are new, not the original ones, so a mistake in either shows up as a difference. The children hold the steps and their results.
close_reason: All children closed. The rerun reproduced the original hmmbuild data (nail-76e419) and fit (nail-62baa5). Commits `9d8f4df` and `85f6793` set nail's single-sequence tau to -(1.34 ln(L) - 2.33), which nail-7c334f and nail-c087ea record.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text:
How this milestone came about, in order, with where each record lives.

1. nail-7cf0cd: `test_hmm_from_blosum62` panicked on a `todo!` left when `036babf` removed the `Hmm` struct. Its lambda half became `blosum62_profile_lambda_matches_hmmbuild` in `b05455b`, and `Profile::calibrate_tau` was removed as unused.
2. To see whether tau could be tested, the note on nail-7cf0cd records a seed experiment. The bag was 48 sequences from `nail-benchmarks/data/swissprot.fa`: the first two made only of the 20 standard residues whose length fell within 3% of each of 30, 40, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 500, 600, 700, 850, 1000, 1250, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000, 4000 and 5000. The bag also held the 7tm_1 consensus. Each ran through `hmmbuild --cpu 1 --singlemx --informat afa --seed S` for S from 1 to 100, and through `Profile::from_blosum_62_and_seq`. Lambda matched hmmbuild within 1.1e-5. Tau varied by about 0.18 across seeds, and nail's tau sat 0.30 above hmmbuild's mean, which became nail-7c334f.
3. Jack supplied the colleague's archive, and this milestone's body describes it. nail-76e419 reran it and nail-62baa5 refit it, each with new scripts.
4. nail-7c334f set nail's tau to the fit in `9d8f4df`. nail-c087ea searched for the source of `KL_BLOSUM62 = 0.589` and found none. The draft paper Jack shared states the fit with no relative entropy term, and says it must be refit for any other scoring scheme. `85f6793` dropped the term.
5. HMMER's `esl_exp_surv` in `easel/esl_exponential.c` returns 1 for a score below tau, and its Forward filter in `p7_pipeline.c` calls it. nail's `p_value` returned more than 1 there, and `eeab798` caps it the same way.

The scratch directories `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-tau-calibration` and `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-tau-lambda-seeds` were deleted on 2026-10-14. The scripts were short, and the issue bodies and close reasons describe what each did. The original archive stays at `~/Downloads/tau-calibration.zip` on the 16-core box.
